newsitem.title: UK: UK life insurers post strong first-half growth.
newsitem.headline: UK life insurers post strong first-half growth.

text.p: Sales of life insurance and pension products continued to grow strongly in the first half of the year according to figures from three leading companies released on Wednesday.
Prudential Corp and Legal & General both reported robust growth in the first six months of 1997, building on the performance in the first quarter.
Britannic Assurance, however, saw sales dip from a year earlier but said that reflected a major restructuring of its field force in the second quarter.

The figures were broadly in line with expectations. But one analyst suggested they could mark an end of the recovery period for the industry which saw sales hurt in 1994 and 1995 due to adverse publicity created by the pension mis-selling scandal and commission disclosure.
"It was the second quarter 1996 when the recovery started in earnest so we're going through a period where sales are back at normal levels," said Goldman Sachs insurance analyst Stephen Dias.

"They were strong sales figures but the first quarter was very, very strong particularly for Legal & General," Dias said. "The second quarter if anything indicates a slowing in a number of areas - the Pru's Jackson subsidiary and in the UK generally for Legal & General."
Pru shares added 7 pence to 620 pence while Legal & General rose 3 pence to 438 pence by midday on Wednesday.
Disappointment at the Britannic figures pushed its shares 11-1/2 pence lower to 802-1/2 pence.

The Pru, Britain's largest life insurance firm, said sales of single premium life, pension and investment products rose 23 percent to 3.6 billion pounds ($6 billion) in the first half while its regular premium sales was up 20 percent to 294 million pounds.
Chief executive Peter Davis described the results as "excellent" and said the group was enjoying sales growth in all its major operations around the world.
Single premium sales grew 15 percent in the UK to 1.8 billion pounds while regular premiums rose 16 percent to 182 million pounds.
Its U.S. subsidiary Jackson National Life witnessed single premium sales growth of 43 percent to $2.4 billion while its annuity sales grew 71 percent to $1.7 billion.
Legal & General which now manages 50 billion pounds worldwide said new UK equivalent premium income in the first six months of 1997 rose 24 percent to 175 million pounds.
The group said its world-wide new equivalent premium income was up 16 percent to 215 million pounds.

Stripping out unit trusts and PEPs, total UK life assurance sales were flat though individual business continued to be strong. Overseas figures were dull, held back by currency effects said Merrill Lynch analyst Roman Cizdyn.

The exception to the strong rise in sales Britannic, saw new regular premiums fall six percent to 18.6 million pounds in the first half, though single premiums were slightly ahead at 65.9 million pounds.

In May, a new field staff structure was put in place which resulted in the closure of more than 60 branches, bringing the number down to 133. It also involved setting up 380 teams with between four and six financial advisers each supervised and led by a sales manager.
"All this represented a significant amount of change and not surprisingly sales in April and May were depressed while changes were being implemented," Britannic said in a statement.
"However, it is most encouraging to report that the number of new ordinary branch proposals received in June was nearly 20 percent higher than during the equivalent period last year".
